newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end higher, feeders sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end higher, feeders sharply higher.

text.p: CME live cattle closed higher and feeder cattle were sharply higher with March 1997 ending up the 1.50-cent daily limit.

Limit gains in CME hogs and pork bellies provided early support to the cattle, with additional support from lower CBOT corn futures. Strong gains in live cattle fueled additional buying in feeder cattle.

USDA's hog report Friday was the primary propellant lifting the livestock markets. The report showed four percent fewer hogs as of December 1 than a year ago. It also showed farmers were liquidating herds rather than rebuilding them.
Traders said commodity funds appeared to be the leading buyers in live cattle futures against light commercial selling.
Forecasts for higher cash trades this week provided underlying support. Traders said cash cattle should trade at $67.00 per cwt in feedlot markets this week, versus $66.00 tops last week.
Live cattle closed up 1.075 to 0.625 cent with February up the most at 65.875 cents. Feeder cattle were up 1.325 to 1.500 cents with January up the least at 68.200 and March up the limit at 68.550.
Feeder cattle had contract highs in all but the January 1997 contract.
